Avian Influenza Outbreak Disrupts Myanmar Poultry Sector

An outbreak of avian influenza reported last week is continuing to disrupt poultry operations across central Myanmar, with both large and small-scale producers experiencing significant impacts on their workforce and site productivity. The Myanmar Agriculture Association stated on Tuesday that at least 14 major poultry farms in the Mandalay and Sagaing regions have reported confirmed cases among workers or livestock, prompting emergency containment measures.

Soe Lin, spokesperson for the association, said, "We are seeing workforce absences of up to 30% on some affected farms due to illness or quarantine protocols. This is slowing down daily operations, including feeding, cleaning, and processing activities." Several hatcheries have temporarily closed sections of their sites for deep cleaning, while others are operating reduced shifts. The association estimates that up to 500 workers are currently unable to report for duty, with the number expected to rise as monitoring continues.

The Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Irrigation has deployed rapid response teams to coordinate containment and testing, and has called for heightened biosecurity procedures at all poultry-producing sites. "Our immediate focus is to limit further spread among workers and livestock," said Dr. Khin Hlaing, an official at the ministry. "We urge all farms to strictly enforce sanitation protocols and monitor workers' health closely."

Analysts warn that the ongoing outbreak could reduce egg and broiler output in the affected regions for several weeks, depending on the duration of site closures and the speed of workforce recovery. "The industry faces a challenging period," said Ye Mon, an agriculture sector analyst. "If the situation does not stabilize soon, prolonged labor shortages could further impact production capacity."
